headline: Masked settlers attacked eight villages in one day.
summary: Israeli settlers attacked at least eight Palestinian villages in the West Bank on Friday, burning cars and olive trees in the middle of the harvest. In Abu Falah, masked men kicked a Washington Post photographer for about ten minutes. Medics treated 14 wounded. The UN counted more than 1,600 attacks from January to August.
cover_answer: The army is supposed to. Villagers say it stood by.
table_question: A referee sees the foul and does nothing. Is it still a game?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Far away, in a place called the West Bank, families were picking olives off their trees, the way you would pick apples. Some men came and set trees on fire and hurt people. Doctors helped the hurt people, and the families say they will go back to their trees. It is far from here, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Only if they hear it. Apple picking, a fire, and the families going back.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script hands them a picture they already own, picking apples, and sets the fire beside it without dwelling. Cantor's work says the vivid image is what frightens this age, so it ends on the doctors and the families going back. Expect "did the trees die?" Some did.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Olive season in the West Bank, where 110,000 families live off the trees. On Friday, masked Israeli settlers attacked eight villages, burning cars and trees. Soldiers are meant to keep order; villagers say they stood by or helped. A referee who sees the foul and pockets the whistle.
8-12.why: Trees, income, fire, referee. One chain, and who enforces the rule.
8-12.why_long: This age tests whether adults apply the rules they announce, so the script runs one chain, trees to income to fire, then names the referee: soldiers the army says condemn the violence and villagers say stood by. Expect "whose side are the soldiers on?" Yesh Din says sometimes the settlers'. The army says it condemns them.

13-17.script: If soldiers watch an attack and let it run, are they part of it? Yesh Din says that happened Friday, when masked settlers hit eight West Bank villages. The army condemned it. Second: the UN counts 1,600 attacks in eight months. When is a pile of incidents a policy?
13-17.why: Condemn and stand by, both on the record. A teenager can carry both at once; a younger kid picks one.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once, and this story hands them a pair: the army condemned Friday's violence, and Yesh Din says soldiers sometimes assist it. Kuhn says arguing is practised against someone honest, so the script leaves the second question open. Expect "what is the US doing?" It condemned it.

5-7.q: Why did they burn the trees?
5-7.a: The story doesn't say. The trees are how those families earn their money, and the families say they will keep going back to them.

8-12.a: Soldiers are supposed to. Villagers say they stood by. The army condemns it.
It's the harvest. Tens of thousands of families live off those groves.

13-17.a: Rights groups say authorities rarely charge them. The army says they fled.
Harvest season, and an election on October 27. AP says attacks spiked.
